analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 1373-2288). The PR changes documentation only: a date bump, a CI shard description, a build-once link, and added test and diagnostic descriptions. No code, workflow, key handling, attestation, authorization or protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threat IDs: T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-011 (provider authorization) only as context. The SSD cache text (lines 1926-1933) restates existing checks (encrypted accounting, epoch fences, owner-only, no-fallback). It does not loosen the TTL, name derivation, scope or purge posture, so the T-041 posture is unchanged.

The release-lane text (lines 1836-1847) says the dev-branch lane calls release-provider.yml with environment dev and secrets inherit, names no secret, and signs with the Developer ID. This is a description of tests, not a change to the workflows. I could not verify the claim against the workflow sources, which are outside the supplied evidence. If the next pass sees workflow changes, it should check them directly.

The diagnostic text (lines 1377-1394) covers batch logit capture into private /private/tmp directories with metadata binding. It says nothing about telemetry, and line 2126 states that tokens, prompts and completions must never go to telemetry or heartbeats. Capture is default-off and gated by explicit flags. The actual code is not in this batch, so whether private-path and permission handling are enforced remains an unverified contract. Opt-in GPU and live tests use owned paths and loopback only.

No security regression or new attack surface is identified from these doc units. Only part of the patch is visible (the excerpt is truncated), so this is not a full review of the PR.
